text:
marta: quick flag from bringup: ranker-v3-large shows NDCG@10 ~unchanged but precision@1/top1 down ~4% vs prod-ranker. noticed in the short-topk slice (topk=5). anyone seen similar with large models after recent candidate pipeline change?
jordy: what changed in candidate pipeline? we recently turned on aggressive substring dedupe in candidate_culler to reduce duplicates. could that reorder items?
marta: yes candidate_culler v2 enabled substring dedupe + html-entity normalize. training data used the older culler (v1) which only did exact-id dedupe.
kai: substring dedupe can nudge the top candidate order if two items are near-duplicates; top1 is sensitive. why is NDCG stable then? maybe ranker still scores relative ordering similarly for remaining candidates, but the absolute top is different.
nina: can you share the eval command and the topk lists?
marta: ran: `./eval/rerank_eval.sh --model ranker-v3-large --holdout prod-holdout --topk 5 --slices short_topk --seed 202`
marta: example diff (prod vs v3):
```
query: "best museums in nyc"
prod topk: [docA, docB, docC, docD, docE]
v3 topk:  [docB, docA, docC, docD, docE]
```
prod had docA first (clicked in gold), v3 swapped to docB first because docA was merged differently by culler (docB and docA considered substring duplicates and docB chosen as canonical).
jordy: interesting. canonical selection policy matters. we should check canonical score heuristics used by the culler. was canonical chosen by length or by recency?
kai: also check HTML entity decoding: if training used decoded titles ("AT&T" -> "AT&T") while new culler leaves entities encoded, tokenization differences can change scores. small mismatches cascade.
nina: quick triage plan:
1) replay the candidate pipeline with v1 behavior (exact-id dedupe + decode html) and eval ranker-v3-large -> measure top1 and NDCG deltas
2) bucket queries by whether their topk includes near-duplicates (levenshtein ratio > .8)
3) compare canonical selection rule (length vs recency) and rerun with swapped policy to see sensitivity
4) run int8 quantized inference to check if quantization amplifies top1 flips
marta: starting step 1 now on small cluster, dropping results in ~10m.
(eval-bot): job 129842 started: rerank_eval.sh --model ranker-v3-large --holdout prod-holdout --topk 5 --slice short_topk --mode replay_v1_pipeline
jordy: if replay matches prod top1, it's clearly pipeline drift. if replay still differs, then model scoring changed due to other onboarding tweaks.
kai: i remembered one more change: we added embed-norm scaling before softmax in the serving stack to stabilize logits across hardware. training didn't have that. could change argmax.
nina: do we have a quick check for softmax temperature/scale sensitivity? maybe run small grid of scale [0.9,1.0,1.1] on logits and see top1 volatility.
jordy: good idea. also quant sometimes causes logit clipping in int8 path which behaves like extra temperature. run a quant A/B: fp16 vs int8 on same pipeline.
marta: results in: replay_v1_pipeline restored top1 almost fully (drop reduced to ~0.6%), so pipeline drift is ~3.4% of the 4% gap. remaining ~0.6% is reproducible even when pipeline matches. int8 increases the remaining gap to ~1.2%.
kai: that suggests two orthogonal contributors: candidate canonicalization (major) + logit scaling/quant subtlety (minor).
nina: recommended fixes:
- immediate: revert candidate_culler to v1 behavior for the next canary rollout (low-risk rollback)
- short term: change canonical selection to prefer doc with highest click-through in history instead of arbitrary substring pick; also ensure HTML entities decoded uniformly in both train and serve
- medium: add a gating eval in onboarding that measures precision@1 on short_topk slice and requires within +/-1% of gold before promote
- long term: add a small calibration test for logits across fp16/int8 paths (temperature sweep) and include quantized path in onboarding smoke tests
jordy: i'll open PR to make culler default back to v1 and add a feature flag for canonical-selection-policy.
marta: i'll prepare the onboarding gating PR + add the precision@1 slice check to the harness. include a debug dump for any query where top1 differs: show candidates pre-cull, post-cull, logits, tokens, and culler reason.
kai: for the calibration test, a tiny script to apply scale to logits and compute top1 concordance: `python eval/logit_sweep.py --model ranker-v3-large --holdout sample --scales 0.9,1.0,1.1`
nina: add this to the eval-bot as a periodic check too. we should catch pipeline or serving changes early.
marta: logging notes for postmortem: root cause was candidate canonicalization policy + inconsistent HTML decoding; quant/logit scaling amplified residual. impact: top1 regressed on short_topk customers with many near-duplicate docs. mitigation: rollback candidate_culler + gating checks + add canonicalization parity enforcement in CI.
jordy: tagging @product-search for visibility, and @oncall-ml.
marta: thanks all, pushing rollback PR and onboarding test now. :rocket:
